items.title: Michael Abene interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003
items.q: a piece I did for Dave Taylor, a bass trombonist for the symphony and big bands, it’s based on two twelve-tone rows.

ctx.x: That’s funny. When you get — let’s suppose you get a commission to write for let’s say a big band, and there’s no guidance, there’s no stipulations. You can write something totally original. Where does the initial idea come from for you?

Well it happens both ways. Sometimes they will give you a specific — now say I want you to write a piece for trombone, or I want you to write a piece to feature it. Now one piece I’m working on now for the Metropole Orchestra again in the Netherlands is to feature their brass section. It’s a closing piece for a big concert in Tilburg in the Netherlands in April. All right so now you know where your focus is particularly. Now what they want you to do, right now it’s something that’s going to be a through composer…

some kind of a thing will just start happening, start clicking. I mean it’s not a Hollywood movie man. It does happen to me this way. It’s like all of a sudden the strings and the band starts playing in the background.
